细菌是什么？都会让人生病吗？: What are bacteria? Do they all make us sick?
认识一个细胞就能生活的小居民，看看它在酸奶、土壤和肠道里的不同角色。: Meet tiny residents that live as single cells, and explore their different roles in yogurt, soil, and the gut.
一个细胞，也能是一个生命。: One cell can be a whole living organism.
细菌不是“小虫子”，也不是病毒。它们是非常微小的细胞生物。许多细菌与我们和平相处: Bacteria are neither tiny insects nor viruses. They are very small cellular organisms. Many live alongside us without causing harm, some help us, and some can cause disease.

细胞膜把内部和外界分开，也参与控制物质进出。多数细菌在膜外还有细胞壁，帮助维持形: The cell membrane separates the inside from the outside and helps control what enters and leaves. Most bacteria also have a cell wall outside the membrane that helps maintain their shape.
DNA携带细菌生长和活动所需的遗传信息。细菌没有像我们细胞那样用膜包围的细胞核；: DNA carries genetic information for growth and cellular activities. Bacteria lack the membrane-enclosed nucleus found in our cells; their main DNA is concentrated in a region called the nucleoid.
这些小结构按照遗传信息制造蛋白质。细菌有自己的核糖体；病毒没有，复制时要借用宿主: These small structures make proteins using genetic instructions. Bacteria have their own ribosomes; viruses do not and must use a host cell’s machinery to reproduce.
图中的小点代表核糖体，不是另一些细菌。: The tiny dots represent ribosomes, not more bacteria.
细菌的角色，要看情境: A bacterium’s role depends on the setting
选一个场景，找找这些小居民正在做什么。: Choose a setting to discover what these tiny residents do.

制作酸奶会使用特定的乳酸菌。它们把乳中的糖转化成乳酸，使酸奶有酸味，也帮助奶中的: Yogurt is made using selected lactic acid bacteria. They turn milk sugars into lactic acid, which gives yogurt its tart taste and helps milk proteins form a gel.
不是随便一种细菌都能用来做酸奶。: Not just any bacterium can be used to make yogurt.
一些土壤细菌参与分解生物残体，让其中的养分重新进入环境。另一些参与氮循环。它们和: Some soil bacteria help break down the remains of living things, returning nutrients to the environment. Others take part in the nitrogen cycle. They work alongside fungi and other organisms.
不同细菌做不同工作，并不是每一种都能分解所有东西。: Different bacteria do different jobs; no single kind breaks down everything.
肠道里住着许多细菌。有些帮助处理我们难以消化的食物成分。有的通常不引起伤害；有的: Many bacteria live in the gut. Some help process food components we cannot easily digest. Some usually cause no harm; certain strains or circumstances can lead to disease.
有益、无害和致病不是靠外形决定的，也不是永远不变的标签。: Helpful, harmless, and disease-causing are not labels determined by shape, nor are they fixed in every setting.
圆的、长的、弯的，都可能是细菌: Round, long, or curved: all can be bacteria
外形帮助描述细菌，却不能告诉我们它是否致病。实际细菌还有更多形状；这里没有按“好: Shape helps us describe bacteria, but cannot tell us whether they cause disease. Bacteria have more shapes than these; the colors here do not indicate whether they are helpful or harmful.
为什么很多地方都有？: Why are they found in so many places?
细菌种类很多，不同种类适应不同环境。它们能随水、尘埃或接触移动，条件合适时繁殖。: Bacteria are very diverse, with different kinds adapted to different environments. They can travel in water, dust, or through contact, and reproduce when conditions suit them. That is why bacteria occur in soil, water, and on living things; this does not mean every place has the same abundance.
许多细菌通过二分裂繁殖：细胞生长、复制DNA，然后分成两个细胞。真实速度随种类和: Many bacteria reproduce by binary fission: the cell grows, copies its DNA, and divides into two cells. The speed depends on the kind and the conditions. Limited nutrients and accumulating waste can constrain growth, so doubling cannot continue forever.
给大人的科学说明与来源: Science notes and sources for grown-ups
细菌是原核细胞生物，与古菌是不同的类群。“微生物”比“细菌”范围更广，还包含微小: Bacteria are prokaryotic cellular organisms and form a different group from archaea. “Microbe” is broader than “bacterium” and includes microscopic fungi and other groups; viruses are non-cellular infectious entities.
主图画的是一颗典型杆状细菌的剖面，不代表所有细菌。DNA形状、核糖体数量、细胞壁: The main diagram is a cutaway of a typical rod-shaped bacterium, not every bacterium. DNA shape, ribosome counts, and wall and membrane thicknesses are simplified, and some structures are omitted. The three settings describe different bacteria, not one bacterium moved between places.
“到处都有”是日常说法，不是每个位置都能检测到活细菌。不同细菌对水分、营养、温度: “Everywhere” is an everyday expression, not a claim that living bacteria can be detected at every point. Bacteria differ in their needs for water, nutrients, temperature, and oxygen; some use oxygen, while others are adapted to environments without it.

放大支撑网。这里只画一类较厚的细菌细胞壁，网格不是它的真实大小。: A closer look at the supporting mesh. This is one example of a thick bacterial wall; the mesh is not drawn at its actual size.
上方是细胞外，下方是细胞内。膜上的蛋白质可以帮助某些物质通过；点按钮追踪一次进出: The outside is above; the inside is below. Membrane proteins can help some substances cross. Use the button to follow one exchange.
紫色线表示折叠的 DNA。周围淡淡的颜色只标出区域，不是一层核膜。: Purple lines represent folded DNA. The pale color marks a region, not a membrane around a nucleus.
两个部分组成一个核糖体。灰线表示信息的传递者 RNA，上方短链表示正在形成的蛋白: Two subunits form a ribosome. The gray line represents messenger RNA; the short chain above represents a protein being made.
先长大一些：细胞利用合适的营养，增加自身的材料。: First, some growth: with suitable nutrients, the cell makes more of its own material.
留意紫色的 DNA：遗传信息正在复制，准备分给两个子细胞。: Watch the purple DNA: genetic information is being copied, ready for two daughter cells.
两份 DNA 分开，中间逐渐形成分隔；不是把一份 DNA 随便剪成两半。: The DNA copies separate and a partition develops between them. One copy is not simply cut in half.
现在成为两个子细胞，各有一份 DNA。条件合适才可能继续生长，画面停在这里。: There are now two daughter cells, each with a DNA copy. Further growth needs suitable conditions; this illustration stops here.

颜色和数量用于辨认结构。拟核周围没有核膜；图中没有线粒体，也没有把鞭毛画成每种细: Colors and counts help identify structures. There is no nuclear membrane around the nucleoid. No mitochondria are shown, and flagella are not presented as structures that all bacteria have.

这是条件合适时的一次代表过程，不是真实速度。许多细菌这样分裂，但营养、水分和环境: This represents one process under suitable conditions, not its real speed. Many bacteria divide this way, but nutrients, water and other conditions limit growth. The picture does not keep doubling.
主图选择一类具有较厚肽聚糖细胞壁的杆状细菌。细胞壁不是膜：肽聚糖网帮助承受内部压: The main diagram represents a rod-shaped bacterium with a relatively thick peptidoglycan wall. The wall is not the membrane: its mesh helps withstand internal pressure, while the membrane acts as a selective boundary among other functions. Some bacteria have an additional outer membrane; some lack a wall. This is not a universal bacterial envelope. The nucleoid has no nuclear membrane, and ribosomes are not membrane-enclosed tiny cells. DNA shape, structural counts and thicknesses are enlarged. The three everyday settings represent different bacterial communities.
局部膜图只示意某些物质通过膜蛋白的路线；真实运输还涉及不同蛋白、浓度差和能量，不: The membrane detail illustrates routes for selected substances through membrane proteins. Real transport involves different proteins, concentration gradients and energy; nutrients do not all use the same doorway. The division illustration highlights DNA copying, partitioning and separation in sequence. Some real processes overlap, and their timing is not given by this animation. Lacking a nuclear membrane does not mean lacking genetic information.
